story_title: As an Event Coordinator, I want to manually add an attendee to an event's registration list on the Organiser's behalf so that VIPs and non-self-registering attendees can still be recorded.

acceptance_criteria.text: The Event Coordinator can add an attendee to an event's registration list by choosing an existing Attendee account by its email address, and can record the attendee's dietary and accessibility requirements; a person without an Attendee account cannot be added.
An attendee can be added even when self-service registration is full.

Given the number of Registered attendees, self-registered and manually added together, has reached the capacity of the venue booking that registration is measured against (see: Configure Event Registration, SPM-64), when the Coordinator adds an attendee, then the addition is refused.
A manually added attendee's registration is recorded the same way as a self-registered attendee.
The Event Organiser can view attendees added on their behalf.

open_questions: DECIDED 2026-10-28: written before the code (test-first) from the story text pasted from Jira, including Kayalvizhi's AC rewording of 2026-10-18 and clarifications #33 and #99, then built on branch SPM-57-Manually-Add-Attendee to this wording. Every case was clicked through in a browser against npm run fixtures:spm57 on 2026-10-28 and matched; no execution block is recorded, as that is for the tester's own run. Every label, message and page address below is the team's to change.

DECIDED 2026-10-28: who adds. Only the coordinator assigned to the event (AC1 'the Event Coordinator'; #33 'provided to the Event Coordinator for processing'), as for Configure Event Registration (SPM-64). The organiser asks the coordinator; the organiser has no 'Add attendee' button (TC06). A coordinator who is not assigned has no Attendees tab at all (SPM-65, TC09).

DECIDED 2026-10-28: where. An 'Add attendee' button on the Attendees tab (S-11), next to the places line. It opens a form 'Add an attendee' on the same page with 'Attendee email' (hint 'The email address of their Attendee account.'), 'Dietary requirements' and 'Accessibility requirements' (both 'Optional.', the same labels as the attendee's own Register form, SPM-51), and the buttons 'Add attendee' (while saving 'Adding…') and 'Cancel'. On success the form closes, the list reloads, and a green alert reads '<attendee's name> has been added to the registration list.'

DECIDED 2026-10-28: when. Only while the event is Confirmed (self-registration's own first rule, SPM-51 AC3, and the only status in which an attendee can open an event they hold a place in), and only while its registration is turned on. Otherwise the coordinator sees no 'Add attendee' button: a blue alert 'Attendees can only be added to a Confirmed event.' for any other status, or the Attendees tab's existing 'Registration is not enabled for this event' alert (TC08). The registration period and the self-service registration capacity do not apply (AC2, #99): the coordinator processes a list the organiser provides, including after self-service registration closes.

DECIDED 2026-10-28: AC3's capacity is the layout capacity of the venue booking registration is measured against (SPM-64's measuredBooking(): the chosen booking, or the event's only active one), counted against registrations that hold a seat (Registered and Attended, SEAT_TAKING - the waiting list and withdrawals do not count). The Attendees tab shows it as 'Venue capacity: <n> · <Venue> (<CODE>), <Layout> layout'. Refusal: 'This event has reached its venue capacity: <n> attendees in <Venue> (<CODE>), <Layout> layout. No more attendees can be added.' When it can't be known (no active booking, several with none chosen, or a booking with no layout), the addition is refused with 'This event's venue capacity isn't known, so attendees can't be added. Choose the venue booking registration is measured against in the Registration settings first.' - not reachable with the fixtures, so tested only by the unit tests.

DECIDED 2026-10-28: field messages under 'Attendee email': empty 'Enter the attendee's email address'; malformed 'Enter a valid email address' (the login form's wording); no account, an account that is not an Attendee, or a deactivated one 'No Attendee account uses this email address. Only people with an Attendee account can be added.'; already registered or attended '<name> is already registered for this event.'; on the waiting list '<name> is on the waiting list for this event.' Moving someone off the waiting list is Join and Respond to Waiting List (FIFO with manual override, #26), not this story. The email is matched ignoring case and surrounding spaces.

DECIDED 2026-10-28: AC4 'recorded the same way'. The same Registration row as self-registration: status Registered, registered now, with the dietary and accessibility requirements, plus 'added by' set to the coordinator (SPM-65 AC4). Someone who had withdrawn is registered again on their existing row, as POST /api/registrations does. The attendee sees it in My Registrations and on the event exactly as a self-registration (TC02), and can withdraw it.

DECIDED 2026-10-28: so the requirements can be checked, the Attendees tab shows 'Dietary: <text>' and 'Accessibility: <text>' under an attendee's name when they gave any, for every registration - self-registered ones too. Nothing showed them before.
RESOLVED 2026-10-28: notifying the attendee that they were added is not in this story's ACs. It is Notify people (SPM-53)'s follow-up, which its own changelog says waits for SPM-57.

RESOLVED 2026-10-29: should the coordinator be able to add an attendee once the event has started or ended while it is still Confirmed? No, from the moment it starts (raised in review; to be confirmed by the team): self-registration closes by the start at the latest, and Join and Respond to Waiting List (SPM-66) stops offering places then. Refused with 'This event has started, so attendees can no longer be added.', shown in place of 'Add attendee' (TC11). An event that has ended is refused the same way; it becomes Completed within 7 days, so no fixture can keep one Confirmed and ended, and that is left to the unit tests.

DECIDED 2026-10-29 (changes the 2026-10-28 capacity entry): since SPM-66 a place on offer to someone on the waiting list is held, so AC3 counts it against the venue capacity with the Registered and Attended seats (placeCounts()). At capacity because of an offer the refusal adds ', counting 1 place on offer to the waiting list' ('places' for more than one) before '. No more attendees can be added.' (TC10).

DECIDED 2026-10-29 (changes the 2026-10-28 capacity entry): an unknown venue capacity is a reason no attendee can be added, shown in a blue alert in place of 'Add attendee' as for the other reasons, rather than an error after the form is filled in. Reachable with the fixtures now (SPM57 Two Room Forum, TC12).

DECIDED 2026-10-29 (changes the 2026-10-28 AC4 entry): a requirement left blank when an attendee is added is recorded as none, so re-adding a withdrawn attendee clears what they gave before (TC13). Registering again through Register (SPM-51) still keeps the old values; that is SPM-51's to change.
